description: Unified Configuration Manifest & Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) File Access Matrix

development_rules.frontend_coverage_policy: CRITICAL: Any feature that adds user-configurable settings (fields in API schema, seller model, or any model exposed to users) MUST include corresponding changes to frontend/index.html in the SAME implementation task. This includes: form inputs, edit population (editSeller/editXxx JS), save payload (saveSeller/saveXxx JS), and table/list display columns. Omitting frontend changes for backend-added settings is a defect and must not happen.

holistic_impact_analysis.policy: REQUIRED: Before implementing ANY change, the agent MUST perform a full project impact scan. The agent must explicitly list every layer of the system that the change touches or might touch, and confirm that changes are applied to ALL affected layers in a single task.
layers_to_scan: app/services/      — Business logic, external API clients
app/celery_app.py  — Beat schedule, task routing, includes
frontend/index.html — All UI: forms, tables, JS save/load logic
docs/              — README, API docs if applicable
required_pre_implementation_steps: 1. Read and understand the user request fully.
2. Search the entire project for all files related to the feature area (models, schemas, api, agents, services, frontend, tests).
3. List every file that will need to change and WHY.
4. Identify implicit side effects (e.g., adding a model field requires: migration, schema, API, frontend form, frontend table, tests).
5. Document findings in the implementation plan before writing any code.

post_change_test_analysis.policy: REQUIRED: After completing any implementation, the agent MUST analyze what tests are needed and implement them. Tests are not optional — a feature is not complete without corresponding test coverage.
required_post_implementation_steps: 1. List every changed or new module/function/endpoint.
2. For each changed unit, identify what behavior needs to be verified.
3. Check tests/ directory for existing coverage — extend rather than duplicate.
4. Write new tests covering: happy path, edge cases, validation errors, and integration with adjacent components.
5. Run existing tests to confirm no regressions introduced.
6. Document which tests were added and why in the walkthrough or task notes.

test_categories.integration: API endpoint + DB round-trip, Celery task execution
test_categories.schema: Pydantic validation rules, field constraints, timezone validators
test_categories.frontend_contract: Verify API response shape matches what frontend JS expects
test_categories.regression: Existing tests must still pass after every change

post_change_test_analysis.test_file_convention: tests/test_<feature_area>.py — group tests by feature domain, not by layer

token_efficient_codebase_indexing.policy: REQUIRED: To prevent excessive token consumption when analyzing the project, agents must NEVER read full files indiscriminately across the codebase. Agents must use the two-tier index (codebase_index.json and CODEBASE_MAP.md) or lookup_code_symbol() for preliminary discovery, and only read specific targeted files when their relevance is confirmed.
token_efficient_codebase_indexing.automatic_maintenance_policy: REQUIRED: Whenever any code or configuration file is created, modified, or deleted, the codebase index MUST be updated via CodebaseIndexer().save_index() to maintain 100% synchronization of all symbols, classes, functions, routes, and tasks.
required_steps: 1. Discover relevant files via codebase_index.json or CODEBASE_MAP.md by symbol/layer/endpoint.
2. Read only the confirmed target source file(s).
3. Implement modifications.
4. Run CodebaseIndexer().save_index() to refresh codebase_index.json and CODEBASE_MAP.md.
5. Run tests to ensure index and code integrity.

implementation_checklist: [ ] Pre-change: holistic project scan completed, all affected layers identified
[ ] Two-tier lookup used (codebase_index.json / CODEBASE_MAP.md) to minimize token consumption
[ ] Backend model fields added
[ ] Schema/validation updated
[ ] API endpoint handles new fields
[ ] Frontend FORM inputs added (frontend/index.html)

[ ] Frontend TABLE/LIST display updated (show new fields in rows)
[ ] DB migration executed (non-destructive)

[ ] Celery worker memory limits and task recycling parameters maintained
[ ] CLI scripts verified for zero host-level dependency and container auto-forwarding

[ ] Instructions & docs updated (DEPLOY_VPS_GUIDE.md, README.md, docs/ if affected)

[ ] Post-change: test analysis completed, new tests written and passing
[ ] Existing tests confirmed not broken
[ ] Data & credentials preserved (no destructive volume down -v, .env protected)
[ ] GitHub sync: changes committed and pushed to remote repository (AnanyevMA/WB_FBS_VRTN)

github_sync_and_documentation_policy.policy: REQUIRED: Whenever ANY code, configuration, database schema, script, or environment variable is modified, added, or removed, the agent MUST perform two mandatory actions: (1) Keep all user guides, deployment manuals, and documentation strictly up-to-date in the SAME task (DEPLOY_VPS_GUIDE.md, README.md, docs/, codebase_index.json, CODEBASE_MAP.md); (2) Ensure all modified and relevant project files are committed with a clear commit message and pushed to the GitHub repository (https://github.com/AnanyevMA/WB_FBS_VRTN) on branch 'main'.
required_steps: 1. Identify whether changes affect architecture, models, APIs, deployment scripts, environment variables, or operations.
2. Update corresponding user guides and instructions (DEPLOY_VPS_GUIDE.md for VPS setup/commands, README.md for overview/quickstart, docs/ for architectural references).
3. Run CodebaseIndexer().save_index() to ensure codebase_index.json and CODEBASE_MAP.md stay 100% synchronized.
4. Run full pytest suite to verify no regressions.
5. Stage changed files, commit with descriptive message, and push to GitHub remote origin main.

data_and_credential_persistence_policy.policy: CRITICAL: During updates, deployments, or bugfixes, user data and credentials MUST NEVER be wiped or reset. Agents must NEVER instruct users to run destructive volume commands (docker compose down -v) or overwrite existing .env files. Standard updates must only use 'git pull origin main' and 'bash scripts/deploy.sh'. Any password or credential management must be done via dedicated non-destructive scripts (scripts/set_admin_password.py) preserving all database records.
required_steps: 1. Never use or recommend 'docker compose down -v' for deployment updates.
2. Ensure scripts/generate_secrets.py never overwrites an existing .env file.
3. Ensure all DB migrations and schema changes are non-destructive and preserve user data.
4. Provide scripts/set_admin_password.py for safe password updates without data loss.

zero_downtime_deployment_and_nginx_rules.policy: CRITICAL: Any update, deployment, or configuration change touching Nginx, Docker Compose, or networking MUST follow zero-downtime and persistent routing rules: (1) docker-compose.prod.yml MUST mount BOTH ./nginx/nginx.conf and ./nginx/conf.d/app.conf; (2) Nginx MUST use dynamic Docker DNS resolution (resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=10s ipv6=off and variable-based proxy_pass $upstream_api) to prevent 502 Bad Gateway upon API container recreation; (3) scripts/deploy.sh must perform non-destructive updates with --force-recreate, explicit health-check polling, admin login validation, and port 80 accessibility verification; (4) Frontend auth error handlers must NEVER mask HTTP 502/503/504 as 'wrong password'.
required_steps: 1. Always ensure nginx.conf contains rate-limiting zones (api_limit, login_limit) and is mounted in docker-compose.prod.yml.
2. Always configure Docker embedded DNS resolver (127.0.0.11) in Nginx when proxying to container services.
3. Ensure deploy script (scripts/deploy.sh) executes health checks against /health before reporting success.
4. Ensure deploy script checks port 80 and verifies admin login with ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env.
5. Ensure frontend JS distinguishes between HTTP 401 (wrong credentials) and 502/503 (server unavailable).

unbreakable_auth_and_credential_lifecycl.policy: CRITICAL: Administrator authentication MUST be 100% resilient and self-healing across updates, redeploys, or config changes: (1) authenticate_user() MUST support multi-strategy verification: stored DB hash (raw & trimmed), master .env ADMIN_PASSWORD fallback with automatic DB hash resynchronization, and automatic bootstrapping/unlocking if the admin account is disabled or missing; (2) Frontend forms must trim username and password inputs to prevent whitespace/copy-paste errors; (3) Password change via Web UI or CLI (scripts/set_admin_password.py) must update BOTH PostgreSQL and the .env file.
required_steps: 1. Never allow admin account to be locked out due to DB hash desync; keep Strategy B .env master fallback active.
2. On admin login, automatically restore is_active=True and is_superuser=True if account was deactivated.
3. Ensure scripts/set_admin_password.py supports zero-dependency host execution with auto-forwarding to Docker (try_docker_forward) and synchronizes .env.
4. Write automated tests for all admin resilience cases in tests/test_auth.py.

agent_resource_and_oom_protection_rules.policy: CRITICAL: On resource-constrained VPS environments (1 CPU / 1 GB RAM), background agents and Celery workers must be protected from memory exhaustion (OOM crashes): (1) 2 GB Swap file MUST be active (enforced automatically in setup_vps.sh and deploy.sh); (2) Celery workers must enforce --max-memory-per-child=120000 (120MB) and --max-tasks-per-child=50 to proactively recycle worker processes; (3) Celery worker concurrency must remain strictly bounded (--concurrency=1 on 1-core VPS); (4) Docker Compose cgroup limits must provide adequate headroom (worker >= 300M, api >= 280M).
required_steps: 1. Check and activate Swap (/swapfile) before building or launching containers.
2. Keep Celery worker task and memory limits strictly configured in docker-compose.prod.yml.
3. Avoid spawning unconstrained background threads or memory-heavy in-memory buffers in agent code.
4. Monitor memory consumption via scripts/check_memory.sh.

cli_scripts_isolation_and_zero_host_depe.policy: REQUIRED: All CLI maintenance scripts executed directly on the host OS (scripts/set_admin_password.py, scripts/backup_db.sh, scripts/check_memory.sh, scripts/deploy.sh) must have ZERO external Python dependencies at top level. They must run with standard library only (sys, os, re, subprocess, shutil, pathlib) and delegate heavy ORM/database operations into running Docker containers.
required_steps: 1. Never put top-level imports of pydantic, sqlalchemy, fastapi, or application modules in host-facing CLI scripts.
2. Implement try_docker_forward() pattern for any script needing access to database models or cryptographic libraries.
3. Provide clear fallback instructions or regex-based config updates when executed outside Docker.
